issues.detail: The Hebrew 'כְּצֵל כִּנְטוֹתוֹ נֶהֱלָכְתִּי' means 'I walk like a shadow when it lengthens' (i.e., as the shadow declines/extends), not '行在祂翅膀的陰影下' (walking under His wings' shadow). The phrase 'כִּנְטוֹתוֹ' refers to the shadow's stretching/declining, not God's wings. The Chinese adds '祂翅膀的' (His wings) which is not in the Hebrew, and misrepresents the subject of the shadow.

The Hebrew 'נִנְעַרְתִּי' means 'I am shaken out' or 'I am driven away' (like a locust being shaken off), but the Chinese renders it as '顫抖' (trembling), which loses the sense of being shaken out/driven away. The comparison 'כָּאַרְבֶּה' (like the locust) is preserved, but the verb nuance is altered.
